text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Before your first session in Kemberi district, remind farmers that the drought-tolerant sorghum seed from the Halvana Seed Trust needs only 350 millimetres of rain to mature. Volunteers should demonstrate zai pits on a plot of at least ten square metres so that every participant can dig one. In the 2023 pilot, 68% of households that adopted zai pits reported a harvest despite the failed short rains. Do not promise farmers that yields will double; the trial plots did not show gains that large. Each volunteer receives two kilograms of seed per farmer group and should record distribution in the green logbook. If a group has fewer than eight members, combine it with a neighbouring group before handing out seed.

passages.source_passage: Since the last board meeting in March 2024, the Saltmere Coastal Warning Partnership has installed 14 new siren towers along the Orvik peninsula. Coverage now reaches an estimated 82% of residents living within two kilometres of the shoreline. The SMS alert system was tested on 9 May and delivered messages to 11,400 subscribers in under four minutes. However, the northern fishing villages of Tarrow and Leys are not yet connected, because the mast contractor did not complete the access road before the monsoon. Evacuation drills were held in six schools, and teachers led pupils to high ground within the target time. The board is asked to approve an additional 38,000 euros to finish the northern masts by December.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Lantern Evening Classes network covered 22 classes across the Dunmoor and Fenwick wards between January and June 2024. Average attendance stood at 71%, slightly above the target of two thirds. Learners who completed the first module improved their reading scores by an average of 18 points on the Brightwater Literacy Scale. Facilitators reported that women outnumbered men in most classes, but no class in Fenwick had more than three male learners. The evaluators found that take-home reading packs were not distributed consistently, and several learners said they never received the second pack. Retention was strongest where classes met in community halls rather than school buildings.

passages.source_passage: By the mid-point of the programme in September 2024, the Kirrabel Savings Initiative had formed 146 village savings and loan groups in the Ostra valley. Members had saved a combined 2.3 million shillings, and 64% of loans were used to start or expand small businesses. Repayment rates remained high, with only four groups reporting arrears longer than thirty days. The evaluation team did not find evidence that group funds were being diverted by committee members. Women make up three quarters of all members, and most groups elect a woman as chairperson. Groups that received bookkeeping training shared out their savings on schedule, whereas untrained groups were twice as likely to delay the annual share-out.

passages.source_passage: The Sahelkin School Meals Programme now serves a daily hot lunch to 9,800 pupils in 41 primary schools across the Boré and Tandiaga districts. Since the baseline in October 2022, average attendance has risen from 76% to 88%, with the largest gains among girls in the upper grades. Cooks are drawn from parent committees and receive a monthly stipend. Food deliveries were not always on time during the rainy season, and in August 2023 eleven schools went without cereal for two weeks. The evaluators note that the vegetable gardens meant to supplement meals have not yet produced reliable harvests. Teachers reported that pupils concentrated better in afternoon lessons.

passages.source_passage: In the second quarter of 2024, the Pashmira Mothers' Health Trust extended clinic outreach to 37 villages in the Varunpur hills, up from 29 in the previous quarter. Community health workers completed 1,240 antenatal home visits, and 58% of pregnant women in the catchment attended at least four antenatal check-ups. Community health workers also trained 85 traditional birth attendants to recognise danger signs. Facility births rose to six in ten deliveries, compared with fewer than half a year ago. No maternal deaths were recorded among enrolled women during the quarter. However, the mobile clinic van was out of service for three weeks in May, and postnatal visits in the eastern cluster did not meet target. The board is invited to discuss replacing the van before the monsoon.

passages.source_passage: During the 2023–24 reporting year, the Clearbrook Rural Water Fund drilled 18 boreholes and rehabilitated a further seven in the Namuli and Okoro sub-counties. Each borehole serves roughly 300 people, bringing safe water within one kilometre of an estimated 7,500 residents. Household latrine coverage in target villages rose from 41% to 67%. Trained pump mechanics now mentor village caretakers in each sub-county. Water user committees collect a monthly fee of 500 shillings per household for maintenance. Two boreholes in Okoro did not yield enough water after the dry season and have been temporarily capped. We have not yet seen the expected fall in diarrhoeal cases at the Namuli health centre, which the team attributes to poor handwashing at schools.

passages.source_passage: In the Marrowfield district, fewer than one in five children aged three to five has access to any form of early learning. A 2022 household survey by the Little Acorns Playgroup Network found that 63% of caregivers had never been shown play-based activities they could use at home. Since 2020, the Network has trained 120 volunteer parents to run weekly playgroups in church halls, mosques and front yards. In many households, older siblings bring younger children to sessions. Playgroups do not charge fees, and attendance is open to every family in the catchment. Children who attended for at least one year scored higher on school-readiness assessments than their peers. However, the current model cannot reach the 14 hill settlements, where no suitable meeting spaces exist.

passages.source_passage: Smallholders in the Upper Tessa basin farm an average of 1.4 hectares, and most rely on a single maize harvest each year. Between 2019 and 2023, the Greenfurrow Field School Network established 52 farmer field schools, each meeting fortnightly on a shared demonstration plot. Participating farmers adopted intercropping with beans at three times the rate of non-participants. Yet the network has not been able to extend into the southern parishes, where extension officers visit no more than twice a year. Lead farmers mentor new members, and graduates frequently start their own schools. This proposal seeks funds to open 30 new schools and to train 60 lead farmers over three seasons.

passages.source_passage: Between 3 and 21 June 2024, the Velmora Malaria Action campaign distributed 62,500 long-lasting insecticidal nets across the Kassanda and Mbeli health zones. Distribution teams registered 31,200 households, and 94% of registered households collected their nets at fixed points. Community leaders accompanied the distribution teams in most villages. Monitors observed that nets were not hung in about a quarter of homes visited two weeks later. In Mbeli, some families said they did not have enough sleeping space to hang more than one net. Village health volunteers will repeat hang-up visits in July, prioritising homes with pregnant women and children under five. Stock reconciliation showed no significant losses at any of the 48 distribution points.
